name: The Haycock

layers.essential_history: [[c:The Haycock is named after the village legend: a man fell asleep on a haycock, floated down the Nene, and on waking asked where he was. Told 'Wansford', he replied, 'Wansford in England?']]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Daniel Defoe recorded the tale in 1724. It may come from Richard Brathwait's poem about Drunken Barnaby, published in 1638.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:The coachman roars: the strongbox has gone from the yard. Barnaby, still damp from his river trip, hands you a soggy note.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The soggy note]]
puzzle.intro: [[c:Each letter has been moved one place along the alphabet. Move each one back a place.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Where was the strongbox carried? (one word)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:It says BRIDGE. Someone carried the box towards the old bridge.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:A note says the box went towards the BRIDGE.]]
support: [[c:Support the village: the Haycock is a hotel and restaurant.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head west, about 110 metres as the crow flies, to the Old Bridge. Walk onto the old stone bridge. Take care of traffic. Keep to pavements and public paths.]]
